subject: Business
title: Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning
description: Learn Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning in one minute.

hook.text: A shoe company that markets to 'everyone who wears shoes' will be outsold by one that targets marathon runners.

buildup.text: STP is the classic framework: segment the market, pick your target, then position for that target.

discovery.text: Segmentation divides a market by needs, behavior, or demographics into groups with shared characteristics.

twist.text: The counterintuitive part: a smaller target often yields a bigger business. Focus creates loyalty and word-of-mouth.

climax.text: Dollar Shave Club targeted men annoyed by expensive razors. That narrow focus built a $1 billion brand.

punchline.text: Narrow your target. Deepen your impact.

quiz.question: What are the three steps of STP?

details.summary: STP is the three-step marketing strategy process of dividing a market into segments, selecting the most attractive segments to target, and positioning your offering to appeal specifically to those chosen segments. It ensures marketing resources focus where they generate the highest returns.
details.whyItMatters: Trying to serve everyone serves no one well. STP focuses limited resources on the customers most likely to buy and most profitable to serve, creating stronger competitive positions in targeted segments rather than weak positions across the entire
takeaways: Segmentation divides the market into distinct groups with shared characteristics
Targeting selects the most attractive and viable segments to pursue
Positioning crafts a compelling value proposition for each target segment

faq.question: What makes a market segment viable for targeting?
faq.answer: Segments must be measurable enough to size, substantial enough to be profitable, accessible through marketing channels, differentiable from other segments in their needs, and actionable with your company's resources and capabilities. All five criteria must be met.

faq.question: How detailed should market segmentation be?
faq.answer: Segment enough to reveal meaningfully different customer needs but not so much that segments become too small to serve profitably. Start with broad behavioral or needs-based segments, then refine as customer data accumulates. Over-segmentation fragments resources.
